title: Methodology Scope-of-Claim — Competence Without Independent Second-Order Critique
summary: States that RDD does not guarantee the agent independently generates second-order critique of its own output: Cycle 10 documented seven failure-mode instances (the agent composes a framing at a synthesis moment and the user follows along without evaluating) and one success-mode instance (the user evaluates the agent's composition against stated criteria) across four phases. The methodology's positive scope of claim rests on competent first-order analysis plus mechanisms that supply second-order critique from outside the in-context agent — Tier 1 specialist-subagent dispatches, conversational mechanisms inviting user second-order engagement, a phase-boundary compound defense, and provenance attribution — so the guarantee rests on those mechanisms firing, not on the agent's independent judgment.
workflow_point: cross-cutting — methodology-level claim about agent second-order critique
mechanism: named positive/negative scope-of-claim distinguishing mechanism-supplied from agent-independent second-order critique
